units.function: Company-scoped HTTP API for decision queues, source membership, triage deadlines/snooze and retention archive/keep controls.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes combine shared validators, route actor state, authorization actions and queue/retention services; authority remains transport-mediated.
units.keyDataModels: Named queue, heterogeneous attention-source reference, triage override, responsible-user attribution and retention state.
units.lifecycle: Board or eligible Agent reads/manages queues, adds readable sources, changes triage metadata and archives/revives attention sidecars.
units.testAssessment: Embedded-Postgres route tests cover idempotent queue creation, actor audit, heterogeneous source visibility, hidden/missing equivalence, seeded queues, concurrent partial triage updates and restricted task-bridge/skill-test credentials. Stable error codes and application-level responsibility enforcement remain inconsistent.
units.designRationale: Give Agents and humans one durable inbox/triage surface over many decision-like source types without moving the source records.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss needs configurable, responsibility-aware work/approval inboxes without duplicating source truth.
units.companyOsFit: The sidecar queue and per-source read check are useful. Company OS should expose one typed Projection API backed by a source registry, stable codes and application authorization; queue mutation must not imply authority to decide the underlying action.
units.responsibilityConflict: The route records on-behalf-of identity but does not require a responsibility contract, and any principal with generic queue-manage authority can reorder organizational attention regardless of accountable role.

units.function: Durable heterogeneous attention queues, source-level visibility filtering, triage versioning/events and data-backed starter-queue materialization.
units.dependencyDirection: Service directly switches across approvals, decisions, interactions, runs, issues, recovery, join and budget tables and calls authorization/activity services.
units.keyDataModels: Queue/item, sourceKind/sourceId, creator/adder/responsible user, triage version and append-only triage event.
units.lifecycle: Resolve source to an authorization resource, create/list/update queues, add/remove references transactionally, serialize triage writes with advisory locks and seed PR/plan/question queues idempotently.
units.testAssessment: Tests exercise primary mutations, source visibility, idempotent seeding and concurrent triage merging. Missing coverage includes high-cardinality performance, deleted-source reconciliation for non-board readers, all attention kinds and source-switch/schema drift. Listing performs per-queue then per-item authorization queries, creating an N+1 scaling path.
units.designRationale: Keep attention organization orthogonal to underlying domain objects while preserving source-specific authorization.
units.companyOsProblem: One Agent Boss desk must project tasks, approvals, failures and data/security alerts without one giant coupled service.
units.companyOsFit: Adopt the sidecar-reference, visibility-before-disclosure, versioned triage and append-event ideas. Replace the central sourceKind switch with registered projection providers and batched authorization; source IDs stay opaque and source lifecycle emits reconciliation events.
units.responsibilityConflict: responsibleUserId is optional attribution copied at queue mutation time, not the accountable human frozen on the referenced work contract.

units.function: Versioned attention retention, exact reviewed archive manifests, TTL archive, keep/revive controls and durable Agent notification outbox.
units.dependencyDirection: Service consumes attention projections, source authorization, Paperclip source schemas, activity log and a heartbeat notification callback.
units.keyDataModels: Retention/version/archiveVersion, source activity cutoff, archive actor/reason, signed-review manifest entry and notification outbox claim state.
units.lifecycle: Synchronize source activity, increment version on drift, preserve Keep, atomically re-authorize and archive an exact manifest, auto-archive idle entries, claim stale/pending notifications and retry at least once.
units.testAssessment: Focused tests prove TTL archive/revive, Keep exclusion, one notification batch per Agent and all-or-nothing stale-manifest rejection. Gaps include notification backoff/dead-lettering, concurrent worker locking beyond conditional update, retry ceilings, every source origin mapping, manual archive event atomicity and tenant policy overrides.
units.designRationale: Treat attention as a lifecycle-managed projection and make bulk cleanup reviewable rather than silently deleting source data.
units.companyOsProblem: Responsibility/evidence/attention records need explicit lifecycle, legal retention, human-reviewed bulk actions and reliable follow-up.
units.companyOsFit: This is the best Paperclip reference for exact versioned bulk mutation and outbox delivery. Company OS should generalize it to policy-specific retention/legal hold, immutable evidence retention, retry/dead-letter observability and signed actor/action receipts.
units.responsibilityConflict: Archiving hides a projection rather than deleting evidence, which is appropriate, but generic board/source-read authority is not sufficient for evidence retention or legal-hold changes.

units.function: Human-only capture, preview, library, note editing, deletion and full-company JSONL export for decision-training examples.
units.dependencyDirection: HTTP layer exposes the snapshot service directly and relies on board/company/author checks plus activity logging; export serializes every example in memory.
units.keyDataModels: Frozen state snapshot, human notes/history, outcome label, author and JSONL state/label records.
units.lifecycle: A board user previews/captures a decision snapshot, edits only their notes, browses records and can export all company examples or delete their own record.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover human-only writes/reads/exports, author-only mutation, immutable snapshot, audit of reads/exports, no-op notes and strict update shape. They do not test step-up authorization, export data policy/approval, size/streaming, rate limits, purpose consent, redaction breadth or concurrent note updates.
units.designRationale: Turn human decisions into reusable labeled examples while keeping source state frozen and user guidance editable.
units.companyOsProblem: Future Agent Boss training/certification may learn from decisions, but enterprise data cannot silently become a model-training dataset or leave through an unrestricted export.
units.companyOsFit: Do not copy this route. Company OS needs a Data Authorization/Export Firewall use case with explicit purpose, field manifest, preview, accountable exporter, approval, digest, streaming and revocation/retention policy before any training-library feature.
units.responsibilityConflict: Any board user can export snapshots containing issue, comments and run records without a data-owner contract or high-risk approval. Author ownership of notes does not establish consent from people whose data appears in the snapshot.

units.function: Captures point-in-time Issue/comment/run/workspace/decision snapshots, resolves a likely code commit, persists labeled examples and scrubs snapshots after source-comment deletion.
units.dependencyDirection: Service reads whole Paperclip DB rows across issues, comments, runs, workspaces and three decision systems, then stores untyped JSON snapshots coupled to those schemas.
units.keyDataModels: Snapshot v1 with full issue/comments/runs, cutoff, decision payload/actor/outcome, approximate commit resolution, notes history and retention marker.
units.lifecycle: Resolve decision cutoff, collect rows last updated before it, infer commit, freeze JSON, deduplicate per source/author, update notes history and redact deleted comment bodies.
units.testAssessment: Strong boundary tests cover cutoff inclusivity, exclusion of later comments/runs/workspaces, comment-deletion scrub, issue cascade, commit-resolution label, uniqueness and snapshot immutability. Missing are schema migration, deterministic canonical digest, field allowlisting, secret/PII redaction, evidence/data provenance, concurrent notes CAS and deletion propagation for run/issue fields beyond comments. Full heartbeat-run rows are copied into the training dataset.
units.designRationale: Prevent hindsight leakage by freezing only information believed available at decision time and preserve code context for later learning.
units.companyOsProblem: Training/evaluation datasets need temporal correctness plus data minimization, consent, lineage and reproducibility.
units.companyOsFit: Temporal cutoff, preview-before-freeze, immutable state/editable label and deletion propagation are excellent design references. Reimplement through governed evidence projections and allowlisted snapshot schemas; never copy entire operational rows or infer authorization from temporal availability.
units.responsibilityConflict: The snapshot omits the governing data contract and copies potentially sensitive operational fields. A recursively discovered commit SHA is not evidence that the selected repository state produced the decision.

units.function: Maps decision/retention continuation events onto Paperclip heartbeat wakeup requests and becomes a no-op when that runtime is disabled.
units.dependencyDirection: Thin adapter couples Decision callbacks to heartbeat vocabulary and payloads.
units.keyDataModels: Agent/issue/decision/outcome continuation and batched archive-version notification.
units.lifecycle: At composition time select enabled wakeup or no-op; on event enqueue a typed automation reason and reference-only payload.
units.testAssessment: Two tests cover disabled no-op and exact decision payload mapping. Retention mapping, idempotency, capability negotiation, missing/deleted Agent, delivery receipt and failure classification are not tested here.
units.designRationale: Avoid accepting continuations when the process cannot own heartbeat execution.
units.companyOsProblem: Paused Connector work must resume through a declared capability without embedding vendor sessions or raw human content.
units.companyOsFit: Reference-only payloads and explicit disabled behavior are useful. Company OS needs a Connector Resume port with idempotency/action digest, capability/version check, timeout/cancellation and delivery/result receipts rather than a heartbeat-specific callback.
units.responsibilityConflict: A wakeup references a decision but does not prove the resumed runtime is bound to the same responsibility/action/data contract.

units.function: Special-case human decision that locks a stalled in-review issue, writes an optional attributed comment and moves it to done or todo.
units.dependencyDirection: Issue-specific service calls issue attention, issue mutation and activity services inside one DB transaction; authorization and wakeup remain in the route.
units.keyDataModels: Issue review-attention state, approve/request-changes action, human note/comment and status transition.
units.lifecycle: Lock issue row, re-check stalled state, persist raw human note as a comment, mutate status and record activity; route then syncs comment and best-effort enqueues resume.
units.testAssessment: Integration tests cover human/operator gates, hidden existence, stale/covered review conflict, row-lock concurrency, attributed injection-shaped note stored as data and reference-only wake payload. The broader route suite also proves an Agent can change reviewPolicy from human_only to anyone in the same verdict patch and then complete the issue, a serious policy self-relaxation gap. Post-commit wake insertion can fail after the decision becomes non-retryable.
units.designRationale: Offer a fast recovery path for reviews whose original interaction/approval path disappeared while preserving user notes as content, not instructions.
units.companyOsProblem: Review recovery must remain possible but cannot become a second weaker approval engine or permit policy self-modification.
units.companyOsFit: Use the row lock, state re-check and reference-only prompt-injection boundary as tests for the canonical Decision engine. Do not create a parallel special-case approval path; resume must use the same durable effect/outbox ledger.
units.responsibilityConflict: Generic non-viewer membership substitutes for designated reviewer authority, the route owns authorization outside the transaction, and policy can be relaxed by the acting Agent on another path.

units.function: Thin browser client for generic Approval list/create/resolve/revision/comment/issue endpoints.
units.dependencyDirection: UI imports shared Paperclip Approval/Issue types and hard-codes REST paths.
units.keyDataModels: Approval, comment, issue and arbitrary create/resubmit payload.
units.lifecycle: Pass browser calls through the common API client without local policy or transformation.
units.testAssessment: No focused test exists for this module; it inherits server/client behavior and offers no typed create schema or stable error mapping.
units.designRationale: Keep page components free of URL construction.
units.companyOsProblem: Independent Web needs generated/versioned API contracts and localized stable errors without leaking backend implementation types.
units.companyOsFit: The module is too thin and inherits the rejected generic Approval model. Company OS should generate a Web client from its own contract and expose precise command DTOs.
units.responsibilityConflict: Record<string, unknown> lets the browser invent approval semantics and provides no compile-time action-contract binding.

units.function: Browser DTOs and REST methods for queue, triage, retention and archive-proposal operations.
units.dependencyDirection: UI imports shared server-shaped types, manually replaces Date fields with strings and hard-codes endpoints.
units.keyDataModels: Queue/item/triage DTO, retention DTO and archive proposal body.
units.lifecycle: Construct encoded paths/query bodies and delegate to the common API client.
units.testAssessment: No focused API-contract test exists. Comments acknowledge server Date types do not match wire strings; hand-maintained DTOs can drift from the server and omit archive actor fields.
units.designRationale: Provide a typed UI facade without placing response DTOs in the shared package.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS Web and future mobile/host adapters need a stable generated contract independent of database row types.
units.companyOsFit: Reference the small facade shape only. Company OS should publish wire-native schemas/OpenAPI/event contracts and generate clients, never patch server Date types manually.
units.responsibilityConflict: The DTO omits much of the actor/provenance surface, so UI display cannot be treated as the authoritative responsibility record.

units.function: Handwritten browser response types and REST calls for Decision list/detail/decide/dismiss/cancel.
units.dependencyDirection: UI reuses shared effect/input specs but locally restates response rows from the server implementation.
units.keyDataModels: Decision state, target snapshots, effect execution receipts and decision filters/input.
units.lifecycle: Build list query, fetch outcomes and post human choice or cancellation.
units.testAssessment: No focused contract test or generated schema guards this 114-line manual mirror. It intentionally omits signedSpec, does not encode stable error variants and includes a legacy childCount field.
units.designRationale: Avoid exposing server response records as a shared product contract while retaining typed page code.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss needs precise approval receipts without coupling Web to persistence rows.
units.companyOsFit: The choice not to expose signedSpec is sound, but manual mirroring is brittle. Company OS should generate a safe projection that includes responsibility/action/evidence digests and structured failure/retry state.
units.responsibilityConflict: The displayed DTO lacks accountable-human origin, authority basis, permission/data contract and evidence bindings, so it cannot answer the complete responsibility chain.

units.function: Browser API for training-example list/detail/preview/create/note update/delete.
units.dependencyDirection: UI imports shared snapshot rows and calls the training REST API directly.
units.keyDataModels: Training target, filters, list item, preview and example.
units.lifecycle: Resolve filters/paths and issue snapshot/training commands.
units.testAssessment: No focused API-contract or sensitivity test exists; the client can receive full raw snapshots and has no field-level disclosure model.
units.designRationale: Centralize URL construction for the training library.
units.companyOsProblem: Governed datasets need purpose-aware views and exports, not a generic browser transfer of operational snapshots.
units.companyOsFit: Do not reuse until the future training goal defines data contracts, redacted projections and export firewall semantics.
units.responsibilityConflict: A board-readable browser response may contain other humans' comments and Agent run data without showing consent or authorized purpose.

units.function: UI helpers for training routes, trainable attention targets and human-readable commit-resolution labels.
units.dependencyDirection: Pure UI logic depends on Paperclip attention and training types.
units.keyDataModels: Attention source/related issue target and commit-resolution confidence label.
units.lifecycle: Map an attention item to a durable interaction/approval-plus-issue target and render route/confidence text.
units.testAssessment: The only test covers two route strings; trainability mapping and every confidence label are untested.
units.designRationale: Hide small product-routing and eligibility rules from components.
units.companyOsProblem: Future training UX must explain snapshot provenance and confidence without presenting guesses as evidence.
units.companyOsFit: The confidence-label idea is useful, but source eligibility belongs in a governed backend projection and must be tested; this Paperclip-specific helper should not be copied.
units.responsibilityConflict: Calling an approximate workspace commit 'resolution' can overstate provenance unless the UI clearly distinguishes evidence from heuristic context.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres integration coverage for queue/triage routes and service seeding.
units.dependencyDirection: Test drives real Express routes and database schema with injected actors.
units.keyDataModels: Queue/item/events, approval/interaction/review sources and triage versions.
units.lifecycle: Seed company sources, perform HTTP mutations, inspect visibility, events and concurrent state.
units.testAssessment: High-value coverage for idempotency, provenance, existence-oracle equivalence, source visibility and advisory-lock concurrency. It uses local implicit board frequently and covers only selected source kinds and small datasets.
units.designRationale: Prove transport, authorization and persistence behavior together.
units.companyOsProblem: Projection/triage contracts require database-backed concurrency and authorization tests.
units.companyOsFit: Reuse the test strategy and adversarial cases, not Paperclip fixtures/types; add scale, every source provider and responsibility-contract assertions.
units.responsibilityConflict: Tests validate optional attribution but not mandatory accountable-human or exact work-contract linkage.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres tests for attention TTL archive, Keep/revive, notification batching and reviewed-manifest atomicity.
units.dependencyDirection: Test integrates retention with the Attention service and actual schema.
units.keyDataModels: Retention rows, archive outbox, review attention and exact manifest version.
units.lifecycle: Create old review items, project attention, archive/revive and assert outbox/transaction outcomes.
units.testAssessment: The stale-manifest all-or-nothing case is especially valuable. Only three cases exist; retry/dead-letter, competing workers, source disappearance and legal-hold policy are absent.
units.designRationale: Exercise retention against the projection that supplies its source version.
units.companyOsProblem: Retention changes must be concurrency-safe and auditable.
units.companyOsFit: Adapt the manifest race and notification batching tests into Company OS retention/evidence suites.
units.responsibilityConflict: No test proves the deciding human has retention authority distinct from ordinary board access.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres/HTTP suite for temporal snapshot correctness, retention scrubbing, access, authorship, immutability and export audit.
units.dependencyDirection: Test spans training service/routes, Attention enrichment and multiple operational schemas.
units.keyDataModels: Cutoff snapshot, comments/runs/workspaces, training example/notes and JSONL export.
units.lifecycle: Seed resolved decision context, capture/freeze, mutate/delete source data, exercise human/Agent access and export.
units.testAssessment: Temporal leakage and deletion tests are strong and reveal the intended privacy model. Missing adversarial payload/secrets, large export, data-purpose approval, concurrent notes, tenant UUID collision and schema-upgrade cases reflect production governance gaps.
units.designRationale: Prove examples represent knowledge available at decision time and remain immutable while labels evolve.
units.companyOsProblem: Training datasets require anti-hindsight tests plus privacy/security governance.
units.companyOsFit: Adapt the temporal/deletion/adversarial access cases after Company OS defines a minimal governed snapshot schema.
units.responsibilityConflict: The tests treat board access as sufficient consent to capture/export all included participant data.

units.function: Unit tests for disabled and enabled Decision-to-heartbeat continuation mapping.
units.dependencyDirection: Mocked callback test has no database/runtime dependency.
units.lifecycle: Invoke adapter and compare exact callback arguments.
units.testAssessment: Clear but narrow two-case coverage; it does not cover delivery/retry/idempotency or retention notifications.
units.designRationale: Prevent runtime-disabled configurations from pretending to resume Agents.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector resume capability must fail closed and be contract-tested.
units.companyOsFit: Use as a minimal adapter-contract example, expanded to version/capability/action-digest and delivery receipt.
units.responsibilityConflict: No responsibility identity or exact approval digest is asserted.

units.function: Integration suite for review policy, stalled-review recovery, human-note isolation, wakeup references and concurrent verdicts.
units.dependencyDirection: Drives the large Issue router against embedded Postgres and a mocked durable wakeup enqueue function.
units.keyDataModels: Company membership, reviewPolicy/execution policy, pending interactions, issue/comment/activity and wakeup request.
units.lifecycle: Exercise Agent/user verdict paths, special stalled recovery and races across several review policies.
units.testAssessment: Strong cases cover hidden existence, row-lock serialization, human-only/not-creator, typed references instead of raw prompt text and stage signoff. One test explicitly accepts an Agent changing reviewPolicy from human_only to anyone in the same completion patch, documenting a critical fail-open self-relaxation behavior rather than preventing it.
units.designRationale: Protect legitimate stage participants while offering recovery for uncovered stalled reviews.
units.companyOsProblem: Approval/review policy must be immutable to the action being governed and prompt-injection-shaped human content must remain referenced evidence.
units.companyOsFit: Carry forward the adversarial note and race tests; invert the self-relaxation case so it must fail and route every recovery through the canonical approval engine.
units.responsibilityConflict: A governed Agent can remove the human-only constraint in the same action it uses to self-approve, violating separation of duties.
